title: Cycle capacity scenarios & rapid-scope-cut playbook
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Playbook and worked examples for allocating product team capacity across cycles, including three capacity scenarios (conservative, baseline, aggressive), a decision tree for mid-cycle scope cuts, and a running checklist for PMs to coordinate with Eng, Design, and Support. The goal is to standardize how we translate OKRs into committed scope, where to cut in-flight work when capacity shortfalls occur, and how to communicate changes to stakeholders and customers.
capacity_model: Model assumptions: 8 PMs, 30 engineers, 6 designers. Velocity baseline: 30 dev points/cycle per engineering pod. Reserve buffer flavors: none (0%), low (10%), standard (20%). Scenarios: conservative = 20% scope held as staging/backlog; baseline = 10% buffer + 5% contingency; aggressive = 0% buffer, prioritized delivery of OKR path. Includes recommended staffing multipliers for feature work vs. platform/ops work (1.6x engineer headcount for platform projects).
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Agreed baseline scenario uses 10% buffer for most product tracks (decision updated after Eng capacity review).
2026-03-04: Design requests nonlinear allocation for discovery-heavy projects (action: allow up to 15% exploratory time in Design estimates).
2026-03-09: Final playbook will require PMs to set a single "commitment tier" per initiative (Tier 1: Must ship this cycle; Tier 2: Nice-to-have if capacity; Tier 3: Backlog).

notes: Guidance summary: 1) Convert OKRs to no more than 3 Tier-1 commitments per product track per cycle. 2) Use the baseline scenario by default; switch to conservative for compliance or hiring churn. 3) For mid-cycle cuts: prefer cutting scope in the 2nd priority set, defer platform refactors that don't block delivery, and never cut security/compliance work. Attach a customer-communication draft when announcing changes. Track net scope moved between cycles in the Cycle Retro doc.
